title: Crime Classics
paragraphs: CBS historical true-crime docudrama created, produced and directed by Elliott Lewis. Lou Merrill’s Thomas Hyland frames independently dramatized crimes drawn from historical records, court reports and newspapers. The frozen GRH archive preserves the 1952 audition, regular CBS programs and a substantial set of AFRS/AFRTS rebroadcast versions.

GRH documents the program through CBS summer replacement run (June 15, 1953 to September 7, 1953) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and CBS regular-season run (September 30, 1953 to June 30, 1954) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Bernard Herrmann (composer on 34 recordings, conductor on 33 recordings, and arranger on 1 recording), David Friedkin (writer on 35 recordings), Elliott Lewis (director on 35 recordings, producer on 35 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), Lou Merrill (host on 33 recordings and performer on 2 recordings), Morton Fine (writer on 35 recordings), Bob Lemond (announcer on 29 recordings), and Ben Wright (performer on 15 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), and [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]] (rebroadcast by).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include family, marriage and domestic murder, murder and homicide, execution, hanging and capital punishment, trial, evidence and historical justice, conspiracy, accomplices and group crime, and assassination and political killing.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Primary-record historical crime reconstruction, CBS sustaining true-crime anthology, Military-network rebroadcast circulation, and Historically suggestive minimalist radio scoring.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|escape|Escape]] (66 shared credited people), [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (55 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (58 shared credited people), [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]] (54 shared credited people), and [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (45 shared credited people).
